claim: Regular exercise has widespread health benefits.
source: Regular exercise has widespread health benefits.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus about exercise benefits.

claim: Regular physical exercise increases quality of life and lifespan.
source: Regular physical exercise has widespread beneficial effects on multiple body systems in healthy individuals and increases quality of life and lifespan.
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about exercise effects.

claim: Exercise is one of the most effective ways of preventing cardiovascular disease through reduction in risk factors such as obesity, hypertension and metabolic syndrome and by enhancing vascular function.
source: It is one of the most effective ways of preventing cardiovascular disease through reduction in risk factors such as obesity, hypertension and metabolic syndrome and by enhancing vascular function (Mann and Rosenzweig, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mann and Rosenzweig, 2012.

claim: Regular exercise reduces morbidity and mortality in conditions such as chronic heart failure and dementia.
source: Regular exercise also reduces morbidity and mortality in conditions such as chronic heart failure and dementia (Sharma et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Sharma et al., 2015.

claim: Intrinsic pathways that mediate cardiac adaptive responses to exercise are triggered rapidly, even after just 1–3 bouts of consecutive exercise.
source: Previous studies show that intrinsic pathways that mediate cardiac adaptive responses to exercise are triggered rapidly, even after just 1–3 bouts of consecutive exercise, and are sufficiently robust to provide significant cardioprotection (Demirel et al., 2001; Powers et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Demirel et al., 2001 and Powers et al., 2008.

claim: Myocardial ROS levels rise transiently during acute exercise.
source: Myocardial ROS levels rise transiently during acute exercise (Muthusamy et al., 2012), which is thought to be related to enhanced activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain during increases in cardiac contractility.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Muthusamy et al., 2012.

claim: Exercise has been found to increase antioxidant capacity in the heart and skeletal muscle.
source: However, these potentially detrimental effects are limited by endogenous antioxidant defences, and exercise has been found to increase antioxidant capacity in the heart and skeletal muscle (Powers et al., 2014; Radak et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Powers et al., 2014 and Radak et al., 2017.

claim: Low-level increases in ROS may themselves induce a response that counteracts oxidative stress (termed hormesis), which represents a physiological adaptive mechanism.
source: Interestingly, low-level increases in ROS may themselves induce a response that counteracts oxidative stress (termed hormesis), which represents a physiological adaptive mechanism (Radak et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Radak et al., 2017.

claim: Nrf2 is a transcription factor which is a master regulator of cellular redox balance.
source: Nuclear factor E2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) is a transcription factor which is a master regulator of cellular redox balance.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about Nrf2 function.

claim: Nrf2 binds to antioxidant response elements (AREs) in the promoter regions of its target genes.
source: It binds to antioxidant response elements (AREs) in the promoter regions of its target genes which include enzymes involved in glutathione biosynthesis and maintenance such as glutamate-cysteine ligase catalytic subunit (GCLC) and glutathione reductase; antioxidant enzymes such as catalase (CAT), thioredoxin reductases (TRXRs) and haem oxygenase-1, and detoxification enzymes such as NAD(P)H quinone dehydrogenase 1 (NQO1) and glutathione S-transferases (GSTs) (Niture et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Niture et al., 2014.

claim: Previous work implicates the upregulation of Nrf2 and endogenous antioxidant defences as an adaptive response to exercise in heart and skeletal muscle.
source: Previous work implicates the upregulation of Nrf2 and endogenous antioxidant defences as an adaptive response to exercise in heart and skeletal muscle (Done and Traustadóttir, 2016; Muthusamy et al., 2012; Oh et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Done and Traustadóttir, 2016; Muthusamy et al., 2012; Oh et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2016.

claim: NADPH oxidase-4 (Nox4) is a member of the Nox family proteins, which generate ROS by catalysing electron transfer from NADPH to molecular O2.
source: NADPH oxidase-4 (Nox4) is a member of the Nox family proteins, which generate ROS by catalysing electron transfer from NADPH to molecular O2 (Lassègue et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lassègue et al., 2012.

claim: Nox4 is constitutively active and is regulated mainly by its abundance.
source: In contrast to other mammalian Nox isoforms, Nox4 is constitutively active and is regulated mainly by its abundance (Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2013.

claim: Cardiac Nox4 levels rise in response to diverse cellular stresses.
source: Previous studies show that cardiac Nox4 levels rise in response to diverse cellular stresses (Lassègue et al., 2012; Zhang et al., 2010), in part as a transcriptional response to ATF4 (Santos et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lassègue et al., 2012; Zhang et al., 2010; Santos et al., 2016.

claim: In the disease setting of chronic pressure overload, the upregulation of Nox4 promotes adaptive cardiac remodelling through effects that include a preservation of myocardial capillary density.
source: In the disease setting of chronic pressure overload, the upregulation of Nox4 promotes adaptive cardiac remodelling through effects that include a preservation of myocardial capillary density (Zhang et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2018) and an Nrf2-dependent enhancement of myocardial redox state (Smyrnias et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2018; Smyrnias et al., 2015.

claim: Myocardial Nox4 mRNA levels increase significantly after 2 bouts of 1500 m moderate intensity treadmill exercise on consecutive days compared to sedentary mice.
source: In mice subjected to 2 bouts of 1500 m moderate intensity treadmill exercise on consecutive days, there was a significant increase in myocardial Nox4 mRNA and protein levels as compared to sedentary mice (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Myocardial Nox4 protein levels increase significantly after 2 bouts of 1500 m moderate intensity treadmill exercise on consecutive days compared to sedentary mice.
source: In mice subjected to 2 bouts of 1500 m moderate intensity treadmill exercise on consecutive days, there was a significant increase in myocardial Nox4 mRNA and protein levels as compared to sedentary mice (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: No change was observed in the expression levels of Nox2 after physiological exercise.
source: No change was observed in the expression levels of Nox2, the other main Nox isoform that is expressed in the heart (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) or in Nox2 activation as assessed by the membrane translocation of its essential regulatory subunit, p47phox, after physiological exercise (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Nox4-null mice had a maximal running distance that was ~60% of that in wild-type controls.
source: This test revealed that Nox4-null mice had a maximal running distance that was ~60% of that in wild-type controls and a maximal running time that was ~65% of that in controls (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Nox4-null mice had a maximal running time that was ~65% of that in wild-type controls.
source: This test revealed that Nox4-null mice had a maximal running distance that was ~60% of that in wild-type controls and a maximal running time that was ~65% of that in controls (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Nox4 has an essential role in facilitating acute exercise in healthy mice.
source: These results indicate that Nox4 has an essential role in facilitating acute exercise in healthy mice.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing reduced exercise capacity in Nox4-null mice.

claim: The ratio of glutathione/glutathione disulfide (GSH/GSSG) was significantly lower after treadmill running in Nox4-null compared to sedentary mouse hearts.
source: The ratio of glutathione/glutathione disulfide (GSH/GSSG), a sensitive marker of cellular redox state, was significantly lower after treadmill running in Nox4-null compared to sedentary mouse hearts (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The levels of 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE) adducts were significantly increased in the myocardium of Nox4-null mice after exercise.
source: Consistent with a more oxidized cellular environment, the levels of 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE) adducts as a marker of lipid peroxidation due to oxidative stress were significantly increased in the myocardium of Nox4-null mice after exercise (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The loss of exercise-induced increase in Nox4 levels results in elevated oxidative stress in the heart after acute exercise.
source: These results suggest that the loss of exercise-induced increase in Nox4 levels results in elevated oxidative stress in the heart after acute exercise.
evidence: This is an inference based on the GSH/GSSG ratio and 4-HNE adduct data.

claim: Myocardial Nrf2 protein levels were significantly elevated after acute exercise in wild-type mice.
source: Myocardial Nrf2 protein levels were significantly elevated after acute exercise in wild-type mice but this response was absent in Nox4-null mice (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and supplementary figures.

claim: The exercise-induced elevation of Nrf2 protein levels was absent in Nox4-null mice.
source: Myocardial Nrf2 protein levels were significantly elevated after acute exercise in wild-type mice but this response was absent in Nox4-null mice (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and supplementary figures.

claim: Wild-type mouse hearts showed increases in transcript levels of the major Nrf2 target genes Cat, Gsta2, Gclc and Txnrd1 after acute exercise.
source: In parallel with the rise in Nrf2, wild-type mouse hearts showed increases in transcript levels of the major Nrf2 target genes Cat, Gsta2, Gclc and Txnrd1 (Figure 1F), as well as increases at protein level (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and related figures.

claim: There was no increase in levels of antioxidant defence proteins after exercise in Nox4-null mice.
source: However, there was no increase in levels of these antioxidant defence proteins after exercise in Nox4-null mice (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and supplementary figures.

claim: No differences were observed between wild-type and Nox4-null mouse hearts at baseline.
source: No differences were observed between wild-type and Nox4-null mouse hearts at baseline.
evidence: This is a statement of experimental observation.

claim: Physiological exercise-induced activation of the Nrf2 pathway in the heart appears to be dependent on endogenous Nox4.
source: Therefore, physiological exercise-induced activation of the Nrf2 pathway in the heart appears to be dependent on endogenous Nox4.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing loss of Nrf2 activation in Nox4-null mice.

claim: csNox4KO mice failed to display an increase in Nrf2 target genes upon exercise.
source: Similar to Nox4-null mice, the csNox4KO animals failed to display an increase in Nrf2 target genes upon exercise (Figure 2A), consistent with a lack of Nrf2 activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: There was no difference between csNox4KO mice and matched control mice in the absence of exercise.
source: There was no difference between csNox4KO mice and matched control mice in the absence of exercise.
evidence: This is a statement of experimental observation.

claim: csNox4KO mice achieved a significantly shorter running distance than matched controls during an exercise capacity test.
source: The csNox4KO mice achieved a significantly shorter running distance and exercise time than matched controls during an exercise capacity test (Figure 2B), with the magnitude of defect being very similar to that observed in global Nox4-null mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: csNox4KO mice achieved a significantly shorter exercise time than matched controls during an exercise capacity test.
source: The csNox4KO mice achieved a significantly shorter running distance and exercise time than matched controls during an exercise capacity test (Figure 2B), with the magnitude of defect being very similar to that observed in global Nox4-null mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Left ventricular fractional shortening (FS) increased by 24% in the control group at peak exercise.
source: While the left ventricular fractional shortening (FS) increased by 24% in the control group at peak exercise, there was a 6% decrease in FS in the csNox4KO group (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: There was a 6% decrease in FS in the csNox4KO group at peak exercise.
source: While the left ventricular fractional shortening (FS) increased by 24% in the control group at peak exercise, there was a 6% decrease in FS in the csNox4KO group (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The increase in FS in control animals was driven by a decrease in end-systolic dimension, indicative of increased contractility, which was absent in csNox4KO mice.
source: The increase in FS in control animals was driven by a decrease in end-systolic dimension, indicative of increased contractility, which was absent in csNox4KO mice whereas there was no difference in the heart rate response between groups (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Treatment with sulforaphane fully restored the exercise-induced increase in cardiac performance in csNox4KO mice.
source: The treatment with sulforaphane fully restored the exercise-induced increase in cardiac performance and maximal exercise capacity in csNox4KO mice (Figure 2, B and C, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1, B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B, 2C and supplementary figures.

claim: Treatment with sulforaphane fully restored maximal exercise capacity in csNox4KO mice.
source: The treatment with sulforaphane fully restored the exercise-induced increase in cardiac performance and maximal exercise capacity in csNox4KO mice (Figure 2, B and C, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1, B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B, 2C and supplementary figures.

claim: Cardiomyocyte Nox4-dependent activation of Nrf2 is essential for the normal physiological increase in cardiac performance during acute exercise.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that cardiomyocyte Nox4-dependent activation of Nrf2 is essential for the normal physiological increase in cardiac performance during acute exercise, which is required to achieve maximal exercise capacity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from csNox4KO mice and sulforaphane rescue experiments.

claim: csNrf2KO mice showed a significant cardiac-specific decrease in Nrf2 mRNA levels in the heart with no change in other organs.
source: The csNrf2KO mice showed a significant cardiac-specific decrease in Nrf2 mRNA levels in the heart with no change in other organs (Figure 3, C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: There was an approximately 60% reduction in Nrf2 protein in the heart of csNrf2KO mice.
source: There was an approximately 60% reduction in Nrf2 protein in the heart (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), with the residual levels in csNrf2KO mice probably attributable to expression in non-myocytes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There were no differences in baseline cardiac size or function between csNrf2KO mice and control Nrf2fl/fl littermates.
source: There were no differences in baseline cardiac size or function between csNrf2KO mice and control Nrf2fl/fl littermates (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Myocardial levels of Nox4 were similar in csNrf2KO mice and control littermates at baseline.
source: Myocardial levels of Nox4 were similar in csNrf2KO mice and control littermates at baseline and increased to a similar extent in both genotypes after acute exercise (Figure 3E), confirming that Nox4 lies upstream of Nrf2.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Myocardial Nox4 levels increased to a similar extent in both csNrf2KO mice and control littermates after acute exercise.
source: Myocardial levels of Nox4 were similar in csNrf2KO mice and control littermates at baseline and increased to a similar extent in both genotypes after acute exercise (Figure 3E), confirming that Nox4 lies upstream of Nrf2.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Nox4 lies upstream of Nrf2.
source: Myocardial levels of Nox4 were similar in csNrf2KO mice and control littermates at baseline and increased to a similar extent in both genotypes after acute exercise (Figure 3E), confirming that Nox4 lies upstream of Nrf2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that Nox4 increases normally in csNrf2KO mice.

claim: csNrf2KO mice exhibited a significant impairment of cardiac function during maximal exercise capacity test.
source: However, when the two groups were subjected to a maximal exercise capacity test, the csNrf2KO mice exhibited a significant impairment of cardiac function (Figure 3F) and a reduced running distance and time as compared to control littermates (Figure 4, D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: csNrf2KO mice exhibited reduced running distance compared to control littermates during maximal exercise capacity test.
source: However, when the two groups were subjected to a maximal exercise capacity test, the csNrf2KO mice exhibited a significant impairment of cardiac function (Figure 3F) and a reduced running distance and time as compared to control littermates (Figure 4, D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: csNrf2KO mice exhibited reduced running time compared to control littermates during maximal exercise capacity test.
source: However, when the two groups were subjected to a maximal exercise capacity test, the csNrf2KO mice exhibited a significant impairment of cardiac function (Figure 3F) and a reduced running distance and time as compared to control littermates (Figure 4, D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: Cardiomyocyte Nrf2 has a critical role in facilitating an optimal cardiac functional response to acute exercise.
source: These results indicate a critical role of cardiomyocyte Nrf2 in facilitating an optimal cardiac functional response to acute exercise.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from csNrf2KO mice.

claim: There were no significant differences between sedentary csNrf2KO mice and littermate controls in respiratory capacity measured as ADP-limited and maximal oxidative phosphorylation.
source: There were no significant differences between sedentary csNrf2KO mice and littermate controls in respiratory capacity measured as ADP-limited and maximal oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOSLim and OXPHOSMax, respectively) (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: After exercise, both sub-maximal and maximal respiratory capacity were significantly lower in csNrf2KO mice compared to littermate sedentary controls.
source: However, after exercise, both sub-maximal and maximal respiratory capacity were significantly lower in csNrf2KO mice compared to littermate sedentary controls (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Neither mitochondrial efficiency (P:O ratio) nor respiratory coupling ratio were altered by genotype or exercise.
source: Neither mitochondrial efficiency (P:O ratio) nor respiratory coupling ratio (an index of the tightness of coupling between respiration and phosphorylation) were altered by genotype or exercise (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: Mitochondrial membrane integrity was similar among groups.
source: Mitochondrial membrane integrity as assessed by the response to cytochrome C in the oxygraph protocol was similar among groups (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Mitochondrial mass, as estimated by the total citrate synthase activity, was similar between genotypes.
source: Mitochondrial mass, as estimated by the total citrate synthase activity, was also similar between genotypes (Figure 3H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Acute exercise resulted in significant increases in the levels of the major mitochondrial antioxidants peroxiredoxin III (PRXIII), thioredoxin reductase-2 (TRXR2) and superoxide dismutase 2 (SOD2) in littermate control mouse hearts.
source: We found that acute exercise resulted in significant increases in the levels of the major mitochondrial antioxidants peroxiredoxin III (PRXIII), thioredoxin reductase-2 (TRXR2) and superoxide dismutase 2 (SOD2) in littermate control mouse hearts (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Exercise-induced increases in mitochondrial antioxidants were abolished in the hearts of exercised csNrf2KO mice.
source: These increases were, however, abolished in the hearts of exercised csNrf2KO mice although there were no differences between sedentary csNrf2KO and control mice.
evidence: This is based on experimental data comparing exercised csNrf2KO and control mice.

claim: There were no differences in mitochondrial antioxidant levels between sedentary csNrf2KO and control mice.
source: These increases were, however, abolished in the hearts of exercised csNrf2KO mice although there were no differences between sedentary csNrf2KO and control mice.
evidence: This is a statement of experimental observation.

claim: A similar abolition of exercise-induced increase in mitochondrial antioxidants was found in Nox4KO hearts.
source: A similar abolition of exercise-induced increase in these mitochondrial antioxidants was also found in Nox4KO hearts (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The Nox4/Nrf2 axis is required for exercise-induced increases in mitochondrial antioxidants.
source: These findings indicate that the Nox4/Nrf2 axis is required for exercise-induced increases in mitochondrial antioxidants.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from both csNrf2KO and Nox4KO mice.

claim: In normal mouse hearts, mitochondrial H2O2 levels were significantly lower immediately upon cessation of peak exercise than in the non-exercising state.
source: We found in normal mouse hearts that mitochondrial H2O2 levels were significantly lower immediately upon cessation of peak exercise than in the non-exercising state (Figure 4B) – consistent with a reduction in ROS at peak exercise due to an enhanced antioxidant state.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B using the MitoB/MitoP probe.

claim: There was no decrease in mitochondrial H2O2 levels with exercise in csNrf2KO mice.
source: In marked contrast, there was no decrease in mitochondrial H2O2 levels with exercise in csNrf2KO mice, in line with the failure to enhance mitochondrial antioxidants.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from MitoB/MitoP measurements.

claim: There were no significant differences in mitochondrial H2O2 levels between genotypes in sedentary mice.
source: There were no significant differences between genotypes in sedentary mice.
evidence: This is a statement of experimental observation.

claim: MitoQ supplementation markedly improved cardiac performance at peak exercise in csNrf2KO mice.
source: We found that MitoQ supplementation markedly improved cardiac performance at peak exercise in csNrf2KO mice and fully restored the maximal exercise capacity in these animals (Figure 4, C to E, and Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C-E and Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: MitoQ supplementation fully restored the maximal exercise capacity in csNrf2KO mice.
source: We found that MitoQ supplementation markedly improved cardiac performance at peak exercise in csNrf2KO mice and fully restored the maximal exercise capacity in these animals (Figure 4, C to E, and Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C-E and Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: MitoQ did not have a significant additional effect on exercise performance in control mice.
source: MitoQ did not have a significant additional effect on exercise performance in control mice.
evidence: This is a statement of experimental observation.

claim: The defect in mitochondrial redox balance is responsible for the impaired cardiac performance and exercise capacity in csNrf2KO mice.
source: Finally, to confirm that the defect in mitochondrial redox balance is responsible for the impaired cardiac performance and exercise capacity in csNrf2KO mice, we performed rescue experiments in which mice were treated with a small molecule mitochondria-targeted antioxidant, MitoQ, for 2 days prior to the exercise capacity test (Smith and Murphy, 2010).
evidence: This is an inference based on the MitoQ rescue experiments.

claim: Cardiomyocyte Nox4 is the physiological driver of exercise-induced upregulation of endogenous antioxidants.
source: In this study, we identify cardiomyocyte Nox4 as the physiological driver of exercise-induced upregulation of endogenous antioxidants, serving to preserve mitochondrial redox state and respiratory function and thereby facilitate optimal cardiac contractile performance and exercise capacity (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a summary inference based on all the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Consecutive episodes of exercise upregulate myocardial Nox4 levels and lead to the activation of an Nrf2-dependent transcriptional program that boosts endogenous antioxidants and mitigates oxidative stress during exercise.
source: We show that consecutive episodes of exercise upregulate myocardial Nox4 levels and lead to the activation of an Nrf2-dependent transcriptional program that boosts endogenous antioxidants and mitigates oxidative stress during exercise.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from the study.

claim: The cardiomyocyte-specific loss of either Nox4 or Nrf2 results in a significant reduction in exercise cardiac performance and maximal exercise capacity in healthy adult mice.
source: The cardiomyocyte-specific loss of either Nox4 or Nrf2 results in a significant reduction in exercise cardiac performance and maximal exercise capacity in healthy adult mice.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from csNox4KO and csNrf2KO mice.

claim: The exercise defect in cardiomyocyte-specific Nox4-deficient mice is corrected by a small molecule Nrf2 activator, sulforaphane, placing Nrf2 activation downstream of Nox4.
source: The exercise defect in cardiomyocyte-specific Nox4-deficient mice is corrected by a small molecule Nrf2 activator, sulforaphane, placing Nrf2 activation downstream of Nox4.
evidence: This is based on the sulforaphane rescue experiments in csNox4KO mice.

claim: The defect in exercise capacity in cardiomyocyte-specific Nrf2-deficient mice can be rescued by a mitochondria-targeted antioxidant, MitoQ, confirming that it relates to a disruption of mitochondrial redox balance.
source: On the other hand, the defect in exercise capacity in cardiomyocyte-specific Nrf2-deficient mice can be rescued by a mitochondria-targeted antioxidant, MitoQ, confirming that it relates to a disruption of mitochondrial redox balance.
evidence: This is based on the MitoQ rescue experiments in csNrf2KO mice.

claim: Nox4 levels in the healthy adult heart are very low.
source: The activity of Nox4 depends on its protein abundance but its levels in the healthy adult heart are very low (Brewer et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Brewer et al., 2011.

claim: An increase in Nox4 abundance is induced by diverse pathological stresses such as hypoxia, ischaemia and haemodynamic overload.
source: Previous studies show that an increase in Nox4 abundance is induced by diverse pathological stresses such as hypoxia, ischaemia and haemodynamic overload (Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2010.

claim: The transcriptional induction of Nox4 by ATF4 was recently identified as an important mechanism for its stress-induced upregulation.
source: However, the transcriptional induction of Nox4 by ATF4 was recently identified as an important mechanism for its stress-induced upregulation (Santos et al., 2016), and it is of interest that exercise is reported to upregulate ATF4 in human skeletal muscle (Drummond et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Santos et al., 2016 and Drummond et al., 2011.

claim: Exercise is reported to upregulate ATF4 in human skeletal muscle.
source: However, the transcriptional induction of Nox4 by ATF4 was recently identified as an important mechanism for its stress-induced upregulation (Santos et al., 2016), and it is of interest that exercise is reported to upregulate ATF4 in human skeletal muscle (Drummond et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Drummond et al., 2011.

claim: Nox4 mediates protective effects in pathological stress situations, such as chronic hemodynamic overload or nutrient starvation in the heart.
source: However, it has been found that Nox4 mediates protective effects in pathological stress situations, such as chronic hemodynamic overload or nutrient starvation in the heart (Zhang et al., 2010; Sciarretta et al., 2013) and angiotensin II-induced remodelling or atherosclerosis in the vasculature (Craige et al., 2015; Schröder et al., 2012; Schürmann et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2010; Sciarretta et al., 2013; Craige et al., 2015; Schröder et al., 2012; Schürmann et al., 2015.

claim: Nox4 was found to specifically activate Nrf2 during load-induced cardiac remodeling.
source: In fact, Nox4 was found to specifically activate Nrf2 during load-induced cardiac remodeling (Smyrnias et al., 2015) and during angiotensin II-induced vascular remodeling (Schröder et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Smyrnias et al., 2015 and Schröder et al., 2012.

claim: Myocardial Nox4 mediates activation of Nrf2 during acute exercise, representing the first physiological function of cardiac Nox4 that has been identified.
source: Here, we show that myocardial Nox4 mediates a similar activation of Nrf2 during acute exercise – representing to the best of our knowledge the first physiological function of cardiac Nox4 that has so far been identified.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the finding, based on the experimental data and literature review.

claim: No increase in cardiac contractility as assessed by fractional shortening was observed in Nox4-deficient mice at peak exercise whereas there was a 24% increase in wild-type animals.
source: Notably, we observed no increase in cardiac contractility as assessed by fractional shortening in Nox4-deficient mice at peak exercise whereas there was a 24% increase in wild-type animals.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from echocardiography measurements.

claim: Nrf2 is activated in the heart upon acute exercise.
source: Nrf2 is a master transcriptional regulator of antioxidant and stress-defense proteins and previous studies found that it is activated in the heart upon acute exercise (Muthusamy et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Muthusamy et al., 2012.

claim: Endogenous Nox4 is an essential and indispensable regulator of myocardial Nrf2 activation during physiological acute exercise.
source: However, here we find that endogenous Nox4 is an essential and indispensable regulator of myocardial Nrf2 activation during physiological acute exercise.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing loss of Nrf2 activation in Nox4-deficient mice.

claim: The absence of Nox4 resulted in redox imbalance during exercise as a result of impaired Nrf2 activation and impaired antioxidant reserve.
source: Therefore, the absence of Nox4 resulted in redox imbalance during exercise as a result of impaired Nrf2 activation and impaired antioxidant reserve, and led to a significant impairment of exercise performance.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from Nox4-deficient mice.

claim: The increased ROS levels in Nox4-deficient mice most likely emanated from mitochondria.
source: The increased ROS levels in this setting most likely emanated from mitochondria (Radak et al., 2013; Saborido et al., 2011), as evidenced by experiments using the mitochondria-targeted redox probe MitoB and the mitochondrial-targeted antioxidant MitoQ.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data using MitoB and MitoQ, supported by citations to Radak et al., 2013 and Saborido et al., 2011.

claim: csNrf2KO mice had a normal heart structure and function at baseline.
source: These animals had a normal heart structure and function at baseline but displayed a significant impairment of cardiac performance and running capacity upon maximal exercise, similar to the phenotype observed in Nox4-deficient animals.
evidence: This is a statement of experimental observation.

claim: csNrf2KO mice displayed a significant impairment of cardiac performance and running capacity upon maximal exercise, similar to the phenotype observed in Nox4-deficient animals.
source: These animals had a normal heart structure and function at baseline but displayed a significant impairment of cardiac performance and running capacity upon maximal exercise, similar to the phenotype observed in Nox4-deficient animals.
evidence: This is based on experimental data comparing csNrf2KO and Nox4-deficient mice.

claim: There was no difference in cardiac mitochondrial function between sedentary csNrf2KO and control mice.
source: Although emerging data suggest that Nrf2 can have multi-faceted effects on mitochondrial metabolism (Dinkova-Kostova and Abramov, 2015; Holmström et al., 2016; Merry and Ristow, 2016b), we found no difference in cardiac mitochondrial function between sedentary csNrf2KO and control mice, indicating that the difference between genotypes was specific to exercise.
evidence: This is a statement of experimental observation, with citations providing context.

claim: An Nrf2-dependent induction of mitochondrial antioxidants is critical to maintain redox balance during acute exercise.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that an Nrf2-dependent induction of mitochondrial antioxidants is critical to maintain redox balance during acute exercise.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from csNrf2KO mice showing impaired mitochondrial antioxidants and redox balance.

claim: Cardiomyocyte Nox4 is the essential activator of the Nrf2-dependent adaptive response, resulting in the maintenance of optimal mitochondrial respiration and cardiac function during maximal exercise.
source: Our study also shows that cardiomyocyte Nox4 is the essential activator of this adaptive response, resulting in the maintenance of optimal mitochondrial respiration and cardiac function during maximal exercise (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a summary inference based on all the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: What is ultimately most important is the redox balance during exercise, especially at the level of the mitochondria.
source: The current study suggests that what is ultimately most important is the redox balance during exercise, especially at the level of the mitochondria.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings of the study.

claim: Targeted antioxidants such as MitoQ that primarily reduce mitochondrial ROS levels may be more likely to have beneficial effects than non-specific antioxidants that might inhibit Nrf2 activation.
source: Targeted antioxidants such as MitoQ that primarily reduce mitochondrial ROS levels (Oyewole and Birch-Machin, 2015) may be more likely to have beneficial effects than non-specific antioxidants that might inhibit Nrf2 activation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental findings and a citation to Oyewole and Birch-Machin, 2015.

claim: Neither sulforaphane nor MitoQ had beneficial effects in the control animal groups.
source: Interestingly, we did not find any beneficial effects of either sulforaphane or MitoQ in the control animal groups, suggesting that there is limited scope for further enhancement of the adaptive exercise redox response in healthy adult mice with normal Nox4/Nrf2 activation, at least in the relatively acute setting.
evidence: This is a statement of experimental observation.

claim: There is limited scope for further enhancement of the adaptive exercise redox response in healthy adult mice with normal Nox4/Nrf2 activation, at least in the relatively acute setting.
source: Interestingly, we did not find any beneficial effects of either sulforaphane or MitoQ in the control animal groups, suggesting that there is limited scope for further enhancement of the adaptive exercise redox response in healthy adult mice with normal Nox4/Nrf2 activation, at least in the relatively acute setting.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of effect of sulforaphane and MitoQ in control animals.

claim: MitoQ did not enhance aerobic training adaptations or skeletal muscle oxidative capacity in young healthy men.
source: This is consistent with prior findings that MitoQ did not enhance aerobic training adaptations or skeletal muscle oxidative capacity in young healthy men (Shill et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Shill et al., 2016.

claim: It is possible that the Nox4/Nrf2/mitochondrial antioxidant pathway could be usefully augmented in older individuals or those with disease-related impairment of this response.
source: However, it is possible that the Nox4/Nrf2/mitochondrial antioxidant pathway could be usefully augmented in older individuals or those with disease-related impairment of this response.
evidence: This is speculation about potential applications of the findings.

claim: Cardiomyocyte Nox4 is a crucial physiological mediator of Nrf2 activation, triggering an adaptive response that maintains redox state, mitochondrial function and cardiac contractile performance to support normal physical exercise.
source: Taken together, these data identify cardiomyocyte Nox4 as a crucial physiological mediator of Nrf2 activation, triggering an adaptive response that maintains redox state, mitochondrial function and cardiac contractile performance to support normal physical exercise.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: The exercise regime used in the study is a moderate intensity protocol.
source: The exercise regime used in the study is a moderate intensity protocol as reported previously (Hafstad et al., 2011; Muthusamy et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hafstad et al., 2011 and Muthusamy et al., 2012.

claim: Exhaustion was defined as the point at which mice spent more than 5 s on the electric shocker without attempting to resume running.
source: Exhaustion was defined as the point at which mice spent more than 5 s on the electric shocker without attempting to resume running.
evidence: This is a methodological definition used in the study.

claim: Sulforaphane was administered at 0.5 mg/kg i.p. 24 hr and 2 hr prior to each exercise regime.
source: In some experiments, sulforaphane (0.5 mg/kg i.p.) or MitoQ (4 mg/kg i.p.) were administered 24 hr and 2 hr prior to each exercise regime, respectively.
evidence: This is a methodological detail from the study.
